fact_text: Pakistan's stock market runs in long boom and bust cycles driven mainly by macro conditions and politics, so long-term investors need a framework for both capturing gains and limiting losses.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'INVEST LIKE A PRO - UNDERSTAND BOOM BUST CYCLES' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Over the 25 years from January 1999 to end-2023 the analyst found the stock market beat other Pakistani asset classes over the long run, but with large ups and downs along the way.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'INVEST LIKE A PRO - UNDERSTAND BOOM BUST CYCLES' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: In the analyst's data the 1994 to 2004 window was a strong equity stretch, with the index returning about 36% a year, while fixed income and gold returned much less in that window.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'INVEST LIKE A PRO - UNDERSTAND BOOM BUST CYCLES' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Asset leadership rotates: after a strong equity stretch, gold became the best performer in the following period, when currency devaluation and a higher gold price arrived together.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'INVEST LIKE A PRO - UNDERSTAND BOOM BUST CYCLES' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Long-run equity returns come in uneven blocks: some five-year windows are nearly flat and others are strong, so the timing of entry and exit matters as much as the long-run average.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'INVEST LIKE A PRO - UNDERSTAND BOOM BUST CYCLES' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: In the analyst's model, strong growth widens the current account deficit, devaluation then lifts dollar-linked assets such as gold, and IMF-backed stabilisation makes stocks look undervalued and starts a rally.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'INVEST LIKE A PRO - UNDERSTAND BOOM BUST CYCLES' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst says aggregate profit of the top 100 companies has grown about 15-17% a year on average, and the index tracks that profit growth while the market P/E causes the swings around it.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'INVEST LIKE A PRO - UNDERSTAND BOOM BUST CYCLES' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Index swings mostly come from changes in the market-wide P/E multiple, which moves with macro conditions, even while the companies' profits keep rising.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'INVEST LIKE A PRO - UNDERSTAND BOOM BUST CYCLES' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: A portfolio can lose value while its companies' profits grow if the market P/E falls; the analyst's example showed a large profit gain alongside a sharp fall in portfolio value.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'INVEST LIKE A PRO - UNDERSTAND BOOM BUST CYCLES' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The primary balance is government revenue minus spending excluding interest on debt; a primary surplus means the state's income covers all of its non-interest spending.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'INVEST LIKE A PRO - UNDERSTAND BOOM BUST CYCLES' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: A sustained primary surplus lets debt-to-GDP fall over time, because the economy grows while debt grows more slowly; this is why the analyst treats it as a key macro indicator.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'INVEST LIKE A PRO - UNDERSTAND BOOM BUST CYCLES' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst reports the stock market rallied in FY24 with the primary surplus as its main driver, after years of primary deficits had pushed debt-to-GDP higher.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'INVEST LIKE A PRO - UNDERSTAND BOOM BUST CYCLES' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst's chart shows the stock index performing better in periods when the primary balance was above zero and weaker when it sat in deficit.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'INVEST LIKE A PRO - UNDERSTAND BOOM BUST CYCLES' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: When the interest rate on debt is close to inflation, nominal GDP grows at about the same pace as the cost of debt, so any real GDP growth pushes the debt-to-GDP ratio down.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'INVEST LIKE A PRO - UNDERSTAND BOOM BUST CYCLES' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: In the analyst's illustration, debt of about 200 bn USD against GDP of about 300 bn USD gives a debt-to-GDP ratio near 67%, showing how sensitive the ratio is to the size of GDP.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'INVEST LIKE A PRO - UNDERSTAND BOOM BUST CYCLES' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst's illustration says that if the current account deficit stays near 2% of GDP and the economy grows about 2%, the dollar debt-to-GDP ratio stays roughly flat rather than rising.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'INVEST LIKE A PRO - UNDERSTAND BOOM BUST CYCLES' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst links falling inflation to fiscal discipline: a primary surplus means less money printing to finance deficits, which helps bring inflation down.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'INVEST LIKE A PRO - UNDERSTAND BOOM BUST CYCLES' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst quotes Warren Buffett's view that interest rates act like gravity on stock prices: higher rates lower the present value of future profits, so the same earnings justify a lower price.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'INVEST LIKE A PRO - UNDERSTAND BOOM BUST CYCLES' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Falling interest rates raise the present value of companies' future profits, so the stock market tends to rise; rising rates do the reverse, according to the analyst's data.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'INVEST LIKE A PRO - UNDERSTAND BOOM BUST CYCLES' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst's worked example: four years of equal profits of 100 are worth about 317 today at a 10% discount rate and about 258 at 20%, so the implied P/E falls from 3.17 to 2.58.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'INVEST LIKE A PRO - UNDERSTAND BOOM BUST CYCLES' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Discounting future profits to present value uses the same logic as a discounted cash flow model, with future cash flows simply replacing profits in the calculation.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'INVEST LIKE A PRO - UNDERSTAND BOOM BUST CYCLES' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst's rule of thumb is that a fair market P/E is roughly 20 minus the country's long-term interest rate, a shortcut he adjusts for Pakistan's conditions.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'INVEST LIKE A PRO - UNDERSTAND BOOM BUST CYCLES' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The 20-minus-rate shortcut works best when interest rates sit in a normal range of about 7% to 15%; at very high rates the formula gives a poor answer.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'INVEST LIKE A PRO - UNDERSTAND BOOM BUST CYCLES' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst argues that with high local rates Pakistan's market is unlikely to sustain a double-digit P/E for long, so a fair P/E in the single digits is the realistic anchor.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'INVEST LIKE A PRO - UNDERSTAND BOOM BUST CYCLES' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst applies a margin of safety and treats a market P/E around 6 to 7 as a reasonable zone when macro indicators are stable and the market is not overvalued.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'INVEST LIKE A PRO - UNDERSTAND BOOM BUST CYCLES' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst says a P/E of about 7 to 8 can be justified when the macro outlook and trend are positive, since the businesses are expected to keep earning profits for years ahead.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'INVEST LIKE A PRO - UNDERSTAND BOOM BUST CYCLES' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst's rule of thumb is to keep at least about half of a portfolio in equities while macro indicators are healthy and the market P/E is below the fair zone; this is the analyst's reasoning, not advice.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'INVEST LIKE A PRO - UNDERSTAND BOOM BUST CYCLES' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst's first rule is not to predict the cycle; act only after macro indicators have clearly confirmed a turn, because early-stage political or economic stories are often noise.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'INVEST LIKE A PRO - UNDERSTAND BOOM BUST CYCLES' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: After an IMF agreement is announced, the analyst's view is that waiting for confirmation is safer than trying to catch the exact bottom, because both bull and bear phases in Pakistan can be long and strong.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'INVEST LIKE A PRO - UNDERSTAND BOOM BUST CYCLES' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst cites the July 2017 disqualification of a sitting prime minister as a clear confirmation point, after which the market moved against the prior trend and offered an exit near the top.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'INVEST LIKE A PRO - UNDERSTAND BOOM BUST CYCLES' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst cites the April 2022 no-confidence vote, when the index fell from a high near 48,000 to about 46,000, as an example of exiting after political confirmation rather than before it.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'INVEST LIKE A PRO - UNDERSTAND BOOM BUST CYCLES' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst's exit approach targets selling within roughly 10 to 15% of the peak, and he said the aim is not to lose more than about 15% from the top.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'INVEST LIKE A PRO - UNDERSTAND BOOM BUST CYCLES' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst warns against predicting political events from early conspiracy-style talk, since such stories are usually at an early stage and only partly true, so acting on them early is risky.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'INVEST LIKE A PRO - UNDERSTAND BOOM BUST CYCLES' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: In the analyst's pattern, when the establishment, courts and opposition all turn against a sitting government, it tends to launch subsidies and import liberalisation to hold support, which weakens reserves and macro indicators.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'INVEST LIKE A PRO - UNDERSTAND BOOM BUST CYCLES' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: In the analyst's pattern, once the government is weakened and an IMF programme is agreed, one to two years of stability usually follow, after which the cycle can repeat.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'INVEST LIKE A PRO - UNDERSTAND BOOM BUST CYCLES' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst treats four main power centres (two large parties, the courts and the military establishment) as the key political input: when they are aligned behind a government, macro indicators hold up.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'INVEST LIKE A PRO - UNDERSTAND BOOM BUST CYCLES' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The current account is decided mainly by exports and remittances, which earn dollars, set against imports, which spend them.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'INVEST LIKE A PRO - UNDERSTAND BOOM BUST CYCLES' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Developing economies cannot borrow dollars cheaply, so balancing the current account matters far more for them than for reserve-currency economies that can print or borrow at low cost.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'INVEST LIKE A PRO - UNDERSTAND BOOM BUST CYCLES' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Pakistan imports large volumes of oil plus LNG priced off oil, which the analyst estimates at roughly 15 to 20 bn USD a year, so higher oil prices widen the current account deficit quickly.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'INVEST LIKE A PRO - UNDERSTAND BOOM BUST CYCLES' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst's chart shows the current account deficit moving inversely with oil prices: when oil rises the deficit widens, which is why oil is a key macro input for the market.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'INVEST LIKE A PRO - UNDERSTAND BOOM BUST CYCLES' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: When dollar reserves fall and the current account deficit grows, investors doubt the economy's staying power, so they pay less for companies' profits years ahead and the market P/E compresses.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'INVEST LIKE A PRO - UNDERSTAND BOOM BUST CYCLES' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst compares a country to a going-concern company: if deficits and falling reserves cast doubt on its survival, investors discount even distant profits of the companies inside it.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'INVEST LIKE A PRO - UNDERSTAND BOOM BUST CYCLES' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst says an IMF programme typically requires a primary surplus and control of the current account; once those hold, inflation and interest rates fall and the market can recover.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'INVEST LIKE A PRO - UNDERSTAND BOOM BUST CYCLES' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst notes interest rates may rise at first under an IMF programme but usually fall within about three to six months as stability returns.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'INVEST LIKE A PRO - UNDERSTAND BOOM BUST CYCLES' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst warns that an IMF window is a chance for structural reform; if those reforms are not carried out, the same boom-bust cycle repeats.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'INVEST LIKE A PRO - UNDERSTAND BOOM BUST CYCLES' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: From more than 20 indicators tested over 25 years, the analyst shortlisted four macro indicators and said no other indicator had a comparably strong link to the stock market.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'INVEST LIKE A PRO - UNDERSTAND BOOM BUST CYCLES' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst says a finance minister's policy success depends heavily on external factors; a sound approach can still look like a failure if conditions turn against it.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'INVEST LIKE A PRO - UNDERSTAND BOOM BUST CYCLES' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst cites 2013 as the stock market's strongest boom in the period he reviewed, a year when a particular finance minister was in office.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'INVEST LIKE A PRO - UNDERSTAND BOOM BUST CYCLES' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst's rule is to act on multi-year cycles rather than on rate-cut or event headlines, because reacting to weekly or monthly news leads to rushed, badly timed decisions.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'INVEST LIKE A PRO - UNDERSTAND BOOM BUST CYCLES' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst observes that investors often exit stocks after losses and move savings to bank deposits, a behavioural mistake that a cycle framework is meant to prevent.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'INVEST LIKE A PRO - UNDERSTAND BOOM BUST CYCLES' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst says about 80% of effort goes into following companies and about 20% into the boom-bust framework, so the macro layer acts as a timing overlay on stock selection.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'INVEST LIKE A PRO - UNDERSTAND BOOM BUST CYCLES' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst argues that if the boom-bust cycle can be predicted, cyclical stocks may deserve more weight than fundamentally strong companies; otherwise strong companies are the more reliable base.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'INVEST LIKE A PRO - UNDERSTAND BOOM BUST CYCLES' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst notes weak companies can sometimes return more than strong ones during a boom, so company-level checks matter even though strong companies win on average.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'INVEST LIKE A PRO - UNDERSTAND BOOM BUST CYCLES' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst suggests reducing exposure early in a bust when valuations are high and the outlook weak, then re-entering on confirmed recovery, starting with the best companies at lower prices.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'INVEST LIKE A PRO - UNDERSTAND BOOM BUST CYCLES' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst's buffer strategy: build a base position first, then add only after one or two years of returns and continued confirmation, so a 10-15% drawdown on a late entry does not wreck the portfolio.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'INVEST LIKE A PRO - UNDERSTAND BOOM BUST CYCLES' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst's best-investment approach compares each asset's expected return over the next three years and reallocates as prices change; when stocks look expensive, gold or foreign markets may rank higher.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'INVEST LIKE A PRO - UNDERSTAND BOOM BUST CYCLES' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst's model portfolio favoured banks on value-realisation grounds, reasoning that their short-term value was not fully reflected in the share price.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'INVEST LIKE A PRO - UNDERSTAND BOOM BUST CYCLES' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Valuation under political risk is subjective: the same macro picture can look cheap to one investor and expensive to another, so the analyst says valuation must be refreshed constantly.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'INVEST LIKE A PRO - UNDERSTAND BOOM BUST CYCLES' (YouTube transcript, undated)
